note:
ISO 2026-W31 runs from July 27 through August 2. Ceres is about 1.1° in ecliptic longitude from Elnath in Taurus. Mars is about 2.9° in ecliptic longitude from Elnath in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Grain Moon — 14:35:43 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. Use β Ara, Rastaban, α Ara, Shaula, Rasalhague, Sargas, Kappa Scorpii, Cebalrai as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -11.8; direct motion; 93.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Jul 29 14:35 UTC. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Jul 29 10:08 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 20.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.2; direct motion; 58.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 93.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 98.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: In solar glare; magnitude -1.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Jul 29 12:17 UTC. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.7; retrograde motion; 99.7% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.4; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Jul 27 06:55 UTC. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Jul 29 10:08 UTC.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** NGC 6352: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Little Ghost Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M14: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Butterfly Cluster: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 6397: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; He 2-290: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; MCG 12-17-9: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

story_candidates.dek: β Ara is a star in Ara of catalogue visual magnitude 2.84; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 2.84. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 17h 25m and declination -55.5°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star does not rise above the geometric horizon. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Ara constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
